title: VLT image of the cometary globule CG4
caption: The cometary globule CG4, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: CG4 · constellation Puppis · about 1300 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #81 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Like the gaping mouth of a huge creature, the cometary globule CG4 glows in this image from ESO's Very Large Telescope.

A cometary globule is a cloud of gas and dust with a dense head and a long, faint tail, so called because the shape can resemble a comet. CG4 looks large and bright, but that impression comes from the telescope. CG4 is actually a faint nebula and is not easy to observe. A large telescope gathering light over long exposures can bring out detail that would otherwise stay hidden.

The exact nature of this globule remains a mystery, and the official caption offers no firm explanation for how it formed or what shapes it. The picture was recorded through several broad colour filters and one that isolates the red glow of hydrogen.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.26 x 7.21 arcminutes) and distance (1300 light years), the frame spans roughly 2.7 × 2.7 light-years. Its light set out about 1,300 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was made with the FORS1 instrument on the Very Large Telescope, using B, V and R filters plus a hydrogen filter. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: CG4 is faint, so it would look nothing like this by eye. The long exposures on a very large telescope make it appear bright.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

alt: The cometary globule CG4, a glowing cloud that resembles a gaping mouth.
